1.0.0: Initial Atlas catalog release of the openspec-orchestrator skill.
1.1.0: Move external OpenSpec store convention to ~/.local/share/openspec/stores/<slug> instead of ~/openspec-stores/<slug>, matching the CLI's own registry location.
1.2.0: Add a fast path for simple, non-breaking fixes that skips extended Propose exploration and drafts straight to critique; present a gate's fixed-choice answer (e.g. Gate 0's accept/revise) as a structured choice (buttons) when the host interface supports one.
1.2.1: No content change; recording via atlas bump going forward instead of hand-editing releases.json.
1.3.0: Add a trunk preflight gate before any change opens, block archive on unchecked tasks until the human ticks them or accepts unverified requirements, add a light lifecycle for fast-path fixes, and give the critic and Verify a fixed input contract.
1.4.0: Run each independent unit of a change in its own worktree and branch with its own standard-tier agent: tasks.md is split into units with recorded dependencies; acceptance checks (unit tests, Playwright screenshot invariants for UI) are committed before code; engine-run iterations are capped at 5 and logged; the critic reviews only green units and must cite their screenshots; a merger rebases units in dependency order before the full gate and Verify. Adds parallel: false single-worker mode.
1.5.0: Route unit workers by role (deep for a unit others depend on, standard for leaves), size each unit critic against its own worker instead of the proposer, run a spec-amending fix round at deep via spec_amend, restate the checker rule as a different model or a different configuration (orchestration.checker_effort), add per-role project overlays in <store>/openspec/roles/<role>.md surfaced by next as overlay: and by roles get, and make Verify warn when a change adds an orchestration key, role, or convention without updating the store's config.yaml.
1.6.0: Under lifecycle light, a non-UI standard leaf unit green on its first iteration merges via unit pass without a unit critic (logged as critique-skipped; Verify still reads the merged diff); default orchestration.concurrency to 2 and unit_concurrency to 3.
1.7.0: Propose classifies every request on four pillars (scope, blast radius, novelty, dependency impact) that decide fast-path, full change, or initiative, and carries a Guardrails line of what the change must not introduce; the critic grades the readings and Verify grades the diff against the guardrails; both appear in the Gate 0 resume.
1.8.0: Add literal engine role prompts with six repeated anchors; next prints prompt: before overlay:
1.9.0: Ship the engine with the skill: the catalog path is now the directory skills/openspec-orchestrator/ (SKILL.md, AUTONOMOUS-ORCHESTRATION.md, CONTEXT.md, scripts/ with run-change, lib.sh and roles/, releases.json), so Atlas installs the whole engine instead of SKILL.md alone.
1.10.0: Add grill mode, replacing /sdd:explore as the only pre-change mode: explore's analysis first, then grilling and domain-modeling write the Project glossary (<root>/openspec/CONTEXT.md) and ADRs (<root>/openspec/adr/), with an external-mode git status guard; the proposer and critic read both, and the critic blocks on an unsuperseded ADR contradiction
1.11.0: Shape before draft: next returns classify (standard) to record the four pillar readings in state, then grill (the in-change grill-mode entry, human interview into the Project glossary and ADRs) for any change not trivial on every pillar, then propose; only state set grill skipped:human bypasses it.
1.12.0: A foundation unit now means two or more direct dependents (a chain link stays standard), split guidance prefers flat splits, and a new orchestration.gate_ui runs browser tests after gate_quick for units in ui_units only.
1.13.0: Gates the engine runs (unit iterate, gate run, trunk preflight) are killed with their process group after orchestration.gate_timeout seconds (default 1800) and reported red with exit 124; role prompts require background commands to carry a timeout, never read bare stdin, and be stopped before the agent returns.
1.14.0: The request's implied baseline (physical law and nature for anything simulated, domain conventions, programming best practice; realistic or silence means natural law, a genre word swaps in the genre's rules) is part of the request: the proposer writes it into the requirements, grill never asks it, the critic blocks a draft omitting part of it, Verify grades it like any requirement.
1.15.0: Escalation by evidence: two consecutive red iterations make the advisor mandatory (unit iterate refuses to run until advisor request --unit has been granted), a red after the advice fails the unit to Gate 1 with fail_reason red-after-advice instead of waiting for the cap, and a worker that finds a check contradicting the spec fails the unit with fail_reason spec at the first red so next gates at once.
1.16.0: Unit size cap (8 files / 3 tasks per unit, store overrides unit_max_files / unit_max_tasks, unit_size_ok exempts a justified unit) enforced by units check, and a Verify floor: Verify never runs below deep nor below the previous Verify round on the change, with next naming the floor when it decides the tier.
2.0.0: 2.0.0: each engine role ships as a Claude Code agent definition (openspec-proposer, -critic, -verifier, -unit-critic, -worker) carrying its effort (high for proposer, critic, Verify; medium for unit critic and worker) and tool allowlist, generated from the role prompts; next prints agent: beside model: so the orchestrator dispatches by subagent_type with the tier model. Includes 1.x: engine shipped with the skill, classify-then-grill, implied baseline, fan-out tiers, gate_ui, gate_timeout, advisor at second red, unit size cap, Verify floor.
